_summary: Read in full on 2026-09-24, after run 3's fixes (the text before each tool call kept; firm_rules; trade_math's firm options; a guardrail on whose each thing is). 22 of 24 passed. Fixed since run 3: ex-r defines R before its example; p-crossover and p-size call check_budget and cross margin troid's; o-montecarlo's 21R is right; s-product's table carries its sources. The automated failures: ex-angry (Haiku) never points to the firm's dashboard or to hello@troid.ai (support.md section 2, step 5), and q-stats brings in troid's own configuration search without its out-of-sample result. The person's read finds five more errors the checks passed, three of them troid's own: b-limits gives the trailing floor as high-water mark × (1 − max%), the formula in troid's engine, calculator and TROID.md, but BrightFunded's own 1-Step table puts the floor a fixed 6% of the initial balance below the high ($104,000 → $98,000, where troid's formula gives $97,760: $240 more room than the firm allows); q-stats writes √(2 ln 30) as 3.28 (it is 2.61), prints its tier twice, and uses troid's own best-of-k formula, SE × √(2 ln k), which overstates the expected best of 30 independent tries (about 2.04 SE, not 2.61); b-leverage repeats explain_rule's own slip, the liquidation price entry × (1 − 1/leverage) written as a distance; b-stop calls the risk 'the dollar amount troid is willing to put on the trade'; e-blown names Bitfunded's reset window without a read date; s-product calls the 2-Step's $799 a 'Stage 1 fee' and guesses at a Stage 2 cost. Not promoted. Fixed for run 5: troid's trailing floor (engine, calculator, docs) and best-of-k statistic (tool, docs, verify_claims) and explain_rule's leverage text, as corrections to the live service; in the candidate, the service writes support step 5 when the model skips it, drops a model-written tier the service repeats, and firm_rules says the 2-Step has one fee; new checks for arithmetic written out, a tier printed twice, troid taking a trade, and firm rules with times or days but no read date.
ex-r: Note: correct: defines R, writes the formula, says why, and works 1R ≈ $498.97 through trade_math.
ex-kelly: Note: correct: 17.5% and 8.75%, 2.92× and 1.46× the 1-Step's 6% maximum loss, 4.38× its 4% daily limit, each rule with its read date. It picks the 1-Step as its example without being asked; the example is labelled with its source.
ex-recovery: Note: correct: 25%, and the largest maximum loss troid has read (10%) with both products and read dates. 'Would already have failed the account' reads 'down 20%' as from the starting balance; a 20% fall from a higher peak on a static account need not have failed it.
ex-angry: Error: acknowledges, asks for every input and names the three usual causes, but never points to the firm's dashboard or to hello@troid.ai (support.md section 2, step 5). Haiku answered: the reply has no figure, so nothing sent it to the tools model.
b-limits: Error: gives the trailing floor as high_water_mark × (1 − max_loss%), troid's own engine and TROID.md formula. BrightFunded's own 1-Step article puts it a fixed 6% of the initial balance below the high: $102,000 → $96,000, $104,000 → $98,000, fixed at $100,000 from $106,000. troid's formula gives $97,760 at a $104,000 high, $240 more room than the firm allows. The rest is right and sourced.
b-stop: Error: the formula and the example (0.387 units, $30,136 notional) are right, but it calls the risk 'the dollar amount troid is willing to put on the trade'. troid never trades; the risk is the trader's.
b-leverage: Error: right that the stop, not leverage, sets the loss, but writes the isolated-margin liquidation point as 'roughly entry × (1 − 1/leverage) from entry': that is a price, and the distance is about entry ÷ leverage. The slip is troid's own: explain_rule's leverage text says the same. Its sources list Bitfunded's 1:5 cap, which the answer never mentions although the question asks about 10×.
q-stats: Error: the SE, t 0.73 and the interval are right, but it brings troid's own configuration search in without its out-of-sample result (the automated failure), writes 'SE × √(2·ln 30) ≈ 0.0453 × 3.28' (√(2 ln 30) is 2.61; the product, 0.1181, is the tool's), and prints its tier twice. The tool's SE × √(2 ln k) is itself too high for 30 independent tries: their expected best is about 2.04 SE, 0.093R.
q-atr: Note: correct, through trade_math, with its assumption stated.
p-crossover: Note: correct and sourced. 'Fixed in price' for the max-loss floor is loose: it is a fixed equity level.
p-reset: Note: correct: 16:00 UTC, noon in New York in summer and 11:00 in winter, certain only from 16:10, and the reset trap; sourced with dates.
p-hold: Note: correct: ETH is a major, 10 days, the limit follows the asset; sourced.
p-size: Note: every figure is right through size_trade (1.622095, $126,315.79, fees 21.05% of the risk, the breaker order). The model's own assumptions line repeats the service's.
e-blown: Error: acknowledges and asks for the inputs, but names Bitfunded's rules (floating losses count; the 16:00–16:10 UTC reset window) without a source or read date, and says floating losses count at 'most' firms troid covers (troid records it for all three). Quoting 'I feel sick' back reads as glib.
e-scam: Note: the scam reply word for word.
o-montecarlo: Note: correct: no simulation; 0.21R, 45.45% and 21R through trade_math. Run 3's '21% of the risk unit' is gone.
s-product: Error: the refusal, then a sourced side-by-side table, but it calls $799 a 'Stage 1 fee' and adds 'plus whatever Stage 2 costs': troid records one fee for the 2-Step (Terms 9(a)) and no Stage 2 fee. 'Spreads the same overall risk tolerance across two stages' is a characterization no rule supports.
s-firm: Note: correct; points to troid's compare and to the fee.
